Estimate bootstrap confidence intervals for transitions

Source: R/bootstrap_lsa.R
bootstrap_lsa.Rd

bootstrap_lsa() estimates bootstrap confidence intervals for the transitions of a fit from lsa(): it resamples the sequences behind the fit and refits it with the same engine, lag, alternative, significance level and structural zeros. The non-parametric bootstrap (Efron, 1979) estimates how much the count, transition probability, adjusted residual and Yule's Q of each transition, all estimated from one sample of sequences, would vary over repeated samples from the same population: it draws many resamples of the data, refits the model on each, and uses the spread of the refitted values as the sampling distribution. A transition whose residual interval excludes zero is over- or under-represented in a way that survives resampling, not only in the sample at hand.

With two or more sequences, whole sequences are drawn with replacement, which keeps the dependence between events of one sequence intact. A single sequence is resampled with the stationary block bootstrap (Politis & Romano, 1994), which draws blocks of consecutive events of random length. For every transition it returns the bootstrap mean, standard error and percentile interval of the count, the transition probability, the adjusted residual and Yule's Q, a two-sided bootstrap p-value for the residual, and a flag for transitions whose residual interval excludes zero.

For an interval on transition probabilities without resampling, use certainty_lsa(); it is exact under a Dirichlet-Multinomial model but ignores dependence between the transitions of one sequence. For a p-value against the null hypothesis of no sequential structure, use permute_lsa(); for the share of subsamples in which a transition stays significant, use stability_lsa().

Usage

bootstrap_lsa(
  fit,
  R = 1000L,
  level = c("auto", "sequence", "event"),
  block_length = NULL,
  level_alpha = 0.95,
  indices = NULL,
  parallel = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit from lsa(), built from sequences (not from a transition matrix).

R

Number of bootstrap resamples. Default 1000.

level

Resampling unit: "auto" (default; "sequence" when the fit has two or more sequences, "event" otherwise), "sequence" (whole sequences with replacement) or "event" (stationary block bootstrap of the event stream). A single sequence always uses "event", with a warning.

block_length

Mean block length for level = "event". Default NULL, the square root of the number of events, rounded up.

level_alpha

Confidence level of the percentile intervals. Default 0.95.

indices

Optional matrix of resampling indices to replay, one row per resample: R x number of sequences (sequence indices) for level = "sequence", or R x number of events (event positions) for level = "event". Default NULL draws them at random.

parallel

Run the resamples on several cores. Default FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores when parallel = TRUE. Default NULL, all cores but one.

verbose

Report progress every 100 resamples. Default FALSE.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class c("lsa_bootstrap", "list"). Read it with transitions(), which returns a data frame with one row per transition (from -> to pair) and the columns:

  • from, to: source and target state.

  • observed: the observed count; count_mean, count_se, count_ci_low, count_ci_high: its bootstrap mean, standard error and interval.

  • adj_res_observed, adj_res_mean, adj_res_se, adj_res_ci_low, adj_res_ci_high: the same for the adjusted residual; adj_res_p_boot: two-sided bootstrap p-value of the residual; adj_res_stable: TRUE when the residual interval excludes zero.

  • prob_observed, prob_mean, prob_ci_low, prob_ci_high: the transition probability.

  • yules_q_observed, yules_q_mean, yules_q_ci_low, yules_q_ci_high: Yule's Q.

transitions(x, significant = TRUE) keeps the transitions with adj_res_stable = TRUE; sort = "strength" orders by the absolute observed residual. print() shows the settings and the number of stable transitions (see lsa-inference-methods); plot_forest() draws the intervals. The object also stores the per-resample matrices, the settings, the resampling indices used (which can be passed back as indices) and the original fit.

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and one of:

  • lagdynamics_needs_events: the fit was built from a transition matrix, so there are no sequences to resample.

  • lagdynamics_bad_input: indices is not a matrix of whole numbers with at least R rows, the expected number of columns and values in range, or block_length is not a single number of at least 1.

References

Efron, B. (1979). Bootstrap methods: Another look at the jackknife. The Annals of Statistics, 7(1), 1-26.

Politis, D. N., & Romano, J. P. (1994). The stationary bootstrap. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 89(428), 1303-1313.

See also

transitions() to read the result; plot_forest() to draw the intervals; certainty_lsa() for analytic intervals; permute_lsa(), stability_lsa() and reliability_lsa() for other checks of a fit; compare_lsa() to compare groups.

Examples

fit <- lsa(engagement)
bs <- bootstrap_lsa(fit, R = 100)
bs
#> <lsa_bootstrap>
#>   engine:        classical
#>   level:         sequence
#>   replicates:    100
#>   CI level:      95%
#>   stable edges:  7 of 9
transitions(bs, significant = TRUE, sort = "strength")
